title: streaming: lifecycle controls - client cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume and server timeouts
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: stabilize streaming lifecycle across client-initiated cancels, abrupt client disconnects, and reconnection/resume flows; surface server-side timeout boundaries for better OpenAI-compat behavior.

Summary: Implements a unified lifecycle control layer in the streaming runtime and API surface: (1) explicit client cancel semantics (graceful stopping and KV cache trimming), (2) robust handling of TCP/HTTP disconnects including server-side graceful termination and short/long disconnect heuristics, (3) reconnect & resume protocol improvements (idempotent resume tokens, partial-chunk resume, and conservative buffer retention), and (4) configurable server timeouts surfaced via API compatibility headers so SDKs and the OpenAI-compat layer can make informed retry/fallback decisions.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add lifecycle controller in runtime that tracks request state and cancel semantics
- [x] Add resume token format and validation (backwards-compatible)
- [x] Implement short vs long disconnect classification to decide KV cache persistence
- [x] Expose server timeout metadata in /v1/responses and streaming headers for SDKs
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + e2e with reconnection scenarios
- [x] Docs: update streaming lifecycle section and OpenAI-compat notes

Compatibility notes: resume tokens are forward-compatible and include a version prefix. Default behavior preserves previous non-resume flows. This change aims to preserve OpenAI-compat semantics while making disconnection behavior deterministic for client SDKs.

If you want to exercise the new flows locally: see examples/streaming-lifecycle/README.md for a small harness to simulate cancels, socket drops, and replay-based resumes.

release_notes: Improved streaming lifecycle handling: clients can now cancel requests reliably, the server classifies disconnects to preserve cache for brief reconnects, resume tokens enable reconnect/resume of partial streams, and streaming responses now include server timeout headers to help SDKs make retry decisions. Backwards-compatible by default; operators can tune tenant-level disconnect windows.
